metadata.description: Hooks, skills, and automations that extend what Claude Code can do out of the box.

plugins.name: audio-transcribe
plugins.description: Transcribe recordings of conversations or talks into clearly documented, speaker-labeled transcripts, fully locally. faster-whisper for ASR (Hebrew + 90 languages) and pyannote for diarization. No audio leaves the machine.

plugins.name: date-context
plugins.description: Injects today's date, day of week, current time, and timezone into Claude's context on every session start.

plugins.name: session-finder
plugins.description: Indexes Claude Code sessions on exit and provides a skill to find past sessions by natural language description.

plugins.name: gdoc-watch
plugins.description: Keep a Google Doc in view for the current Claude Code session: ask questions about it while you edit and get told what changed since you last asked. Pull-on-prompt via gws — no polling, no background watcher. Session-scoped state, snapshot-based diffs.

plugins.name: md-to-gdoc
plugins.description: Convert markdown documents into properly formatted Google Docs using the Google Workspace CLI (gws). Supports custom format profiles extracted from reference Google Docs.

plugins.name: notebooklm-upload
plugins.description: Batch upload local files from directories to Google NotebookLM notebooks. Supports filtering by file type, multiple directories, and dry-run mode.

plugins.name: timewatch-fill
plugins.description: Fill TimeWatch attendance via browser automation with claude-in-chrome. Supports filling a single day, a week, or an entire month of unfilled workdays.

plugins.name: validate-in-chrome
plugins.description: Validate a freshly-implemented feature against behavioral acceptance criteria by driving the user's real Chrome session (claude-in-chrome MCP) inside an isolated subagent. The main agent synthesizes the spec from session context; the subagent verifies sequentially and returns a terse pass/fail summary.

plugins.name: what-i-learned-today
plugins.description: Summarize what you learned across your Claude Code sessions in a given day (or window) as a 10-bullet lessons-learned digest, save it to disk, and run an interactive open-recall quiz. Excludes its own prior output to avoid recycling. Includes morning-recall: a short, confidence-building quiz on the previous days with a spaced-repetition ledger.

plugins.name: session-reconciler
plugins.description: Attributes an uncommitted working tree back to the parallel Claude Code sessions that produced it, from the JSONL transcripts. Mechanical-first (jq) attribution, collision matrix for last-writer-wins risk zones, and a suggested per-feature commit grouping. Never runs git.

plugins.name: worktree-manager
plugins.description: Manage persistent git worktrees for parallel human+AI development across sessions. Create, list, and remove sibling-directory worktrees, auto-detect worktree context on session start, and merge worktree branches back with dependency-ordered, conflict-aware resolution.

plugins.name: session-handoff
plugins.description: Rewrite a repo's session handoff document so the next session resumes from a fresh clone without asking anything. Audits the gitignored state — .env files, CLI pins, virtualenvs — that is invisible in a new directory and fails confusingly rather than obviously.

plugins.name: clip
plugins.description: Put a value straight onto your clipboard with a shell command instead of copying it out of the chat. Secrets from .env files or 1Password are copied without ever being printed; the clipboard is verified by shape, never by content.

plugins.name: session-archive
plugins.description: Hide Claude Code sessions from the /resume picker without deleting them, and restore them later. Matches sessions by name or id, refuses to move a live session, and keeps archived transcripts safe from automatic retention cleanup.

plugins.name: permissions-master
plugins.description: Configure, audit, and troubleshoot Claude Code permissions: rule syntax, tool-specific patterns, permission modes, settings precedence, and the common mistakes that make a rule silently not match.

plugins.name: explain-term
plugins.description: Explain any concept across five fixed dimensions: analogy, mechanism, use-case, the wrong mental model to preempt, and etymology with pronunciation. Volatile terms are verified against live sources; optionally persisted as a glossary file.
